row-20541: On 24 July 2026, dozens of Palestinian rioters clashed with 50 Israeli settler rioters (some armed), accompanied by Israeli forces, on the outskirts of Till (Nablus, West Bank) to take an illegal hike in the area (which is in Area A and B territories). The Palestinian rioters came out of their houses near the town mosque and hurled stones at the settlers after they attacked residents and attempted to break into 2 houses and set them ablaze. Some of the settlers were emergency squad members who were dispatched to the area. Israeli forces then split into two groups, one to deal with one of the injured settlers and the other to repel the rioters. Israeli settlers and Israeli forces then opened fire at the Palestinian rioters, killing 4 Palestinians and injuring 4 others (three of whom were killed in the crossfire). Two settlers were also injured. During the clashes, one of the rioters seized the rifle of an Israeli settler and opened fire with it, killing an emergency squad member and an Israeli 411th Battalion soldier. The rioter is one of the 4 rioters who were killed; he was killed by an IDF soldier. Israeli forces also fired tear gas canisters and stun grenades to disperse the rioters, causing several to suffer from tear gas inhalation. Three of the injured Palestinians were in critical condition and were hospitalized. Israeli Duvdevan forces later raided the hospital they were in, in Nablus city, and arrested two of the rioters involved. The IDF opened a multi-organizational situation assessment led by the Central Command, and the IDF's chief of staff promised that 'he would hunt down every Palestinian involved in the clash'. There were a total of two clashes between the Palestinian rioters and the settlers. Fatalities 6 (4 Palestinians, 2 Israelis). Following an IDF investigation, it was concluded that 'it is not possible to determine unequivocally' the reason for shooting the Israeli emergency squad member that was killed during the incident, unable to rule out the possibility that the squad member was shot by Israeli soldiers during the incident. While the squad member was shot by a rioter who seized his firearm, it is also likely that he was also shot by a soldier during the clash. The IDF also added that the hike was not coordinated or approved by Israeli security agencies. The IDF's Samaria Brigade received preliminary information about the hike only a few hours prior it's beginning and it was determined that Israeli forces joined the hikers late and was unable to obtain details on the route or contact the organizers, and that forces did not respond to the clash with Palestinians with enough forces and that they 'did not act optimally to develop a complete situational picture, dispatch additional forces, and deploy medical teams as required.'
